messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the embedding model swap this morning we're seeing a small but steady spike of 500s coming from the embedding cache layer (redis). Looks like a dimension/hash change so existing cache keys are being treated as malformed and we error out.

devin: I saw that alert. 500s are localized to a subset of tenants (mostly older tenants that haven't touched embeddings in a few months).

eli: Can we just add a read-side shim that detects old-format entries and regenerates them lazily on read? That avoids a big backfill and spreads cost.

maya: That's the lazy migration option. Pros: low immediate cost, no big job. Cons: potentially higher p95 latency for first reads and uneven load spikes if many clients hit cold keys.

sanju: Alternative is a full backfill job that iterates keys and rewrites them to the new format. Pros: predictable latency for clients after job completes. Cons: one-time heavy compute + embedding calls and could be expensive.

qa-alex: Also need to think about correctness: some old entries were stored with metadata we no longer trust (schema v1 had optional normalizers). If we backfill we should validate and maybe trash corrupted ones.

devin: Proposed hybrid: implement a short-term read shim that avoids throwing 500s (fallback to compute on miss) and run a throttled backfill for tenants with >X stale keys. That keeps user experience acceptable while we do the cleanup.

maya: Implementation sketch for shim (pseudo):
```
# on cache read
entry = redis.get(key)
if not entry: return compute_and_store()
if entry.format_version != CURRENT_FMT:
    try:
        rebuilt = translate_old_entry(entry)  # may call small local transform or recompute embedding
        if rebuilt: redis.set(key, rebuilt)
        return rebuilt or compute_and_store()
    except BadEntryError:
        log.warn("bad cache entry, recomputing", key=key)
        return compute_and_store()
return entry.value
```

eli: For translate_old_entry: if the old entry contains the raw input we can re-embed without calling external model. If it only has vector bytes with old dims, then we must recompute via embedding model.

sanju: Important: rate-limit recompute paths and add a circuit breaker per-tenant so backfills or lazy-migrates don't DDOS the model cluster. Suggest token bucket + concurrent-job cap.

devin: Backfill operational plan:
- produce list of tenants with stale-ratio > 5%
- schedule backfill workers per-tenant at low-traffic hours (use k8s cronjob / worker queue)
- throttle embedding calls to X req/s per-tenant and global cap Y req/s
- retry with exponential backoff for transient model errors
- emit metrics: keys_processed, keys_rewritten, recompute_count, errors

qa-alex: Tests: unit test translate_old_entry with several malformed payloads, integration test on staging with 100k keys, run canary on 2 tenants first. Add end-to-end perf checks to ensure p95 doesn't spike > 2x during canary.

maya: UX & comms: send notice to customers we know are affected (CS to own). Add a tenant opt-out flag for backfill if they don't want us to recompute embeddings automatically. Default is opt-in.

devin: Rollout timeline idea:
- Today: deploy non-blocking shim that prevents 500s and logs telemetry (canary on infra nodes)
- +2 days: run small canary backfill for 2 tenants (sanity + perf)
- +7 days: start wider backfill for tenants above threshold, continue lazy-migration concurrently

sanju: Who owns the backfill job? emp-infra + models infra coordination. We'll need a short runbook for throttles and kill-switch (ops-bot integration).

ops-bot: Reminder: create incident ticket if 5xx rate > 0.5% for 30m after shim deployed.

eli: One more tradeoff: cost estimate for backfill vs expected on-read recompute. I'll do a quick calc and post numbers (embeddings calls * cost).

maya: Perfect. I'll open a PR for the shim with the pseudo above and a feature flag behind `embedding-cache-compat-mode`. Devin + Sanju can own the backfill job. QA will validate canary.

devin: I'll also add telemetry events: `cache_entry_malformed`, `cache_entry_repaired_lazy`, `cache_entry_rewritten_backfill`. That will help measure which approach is doing the work.

qa-alex: Happy to run the staging backfill once you have the worker image. I'll prepare test keysets.

maya: Thanks all — action items: PR for shim + feature flag (maya), backfill prototype and cost estimate (eli/devin), canary plan + runbook (sanju/qa-alex). We'll reconvene after canary results. :thumbsup:
